methodology_note: Guard-symmetry audit across the Beanstalk diamond. Two guard families: (1) ReentrancyGuard.nonReentrant, backed by the SHARED diamond slot s.sys.reentrantStatus (cross-facet, not per-facet) and (2) the Invariable solvency/flow modifiers (fundsSafu, noNetFlow, noOutFlow, oneOutFlow, noSupplyChange, noSupplyIncrease). Because the reentrancy flag is shared diamond storage, the absence of nonReentrant on the arbitrary-call wrappers (Farm/Depot/Tractor) does NOT bypass the guards on the sensitive silo/convert facets a Pipeline/blueprint callback would re-enter (those still set/honor the shared flag) — that classic-reentrancy framing is covered by RE-001 and is downgraded here. The reportable semantic asymmetry is in the Invariable family: TractorFacet is the only fund-executing batch entrypoint that does not inherit Invariable and therefore omits the wrapper-level fundsSafu net that its sibling FarmFacet applies. Intra-facet nonReentrant asymmetries (safeTransferFrom, mow, setApprovalForAll) were traced and found transitively guarded or non-reentrant.

findings.title: TractorFacet omits Invariable fundsSafu net that sibling entrypoints enforce
findings.recommendation: Make TractorFacet inherit Invariable and wrap tractor() with fundsSafu (and noSupplyIncrease as FarmFacet/DepotFacet do), so the publisher-delegated batch is subject to the same batch-level solvency net as farm()/pipe(). Alternatively, audit-enumerate every diamond selector reachable from a blueprint and prove each fund-moving one carries its own fundsSafu.
findings.description: Beanstalk applies a consistent guard architecture: every external writing facet inherits `Invariable` and wraps fund-touching logic in solvency/flow modifiers. The two arbitrary/batch execution wrappers FarmFacet (`farm`, `advancedFarm`) and DepotFacet (`pipe`, `multiPipe`, `advancedPipe`, `etherPipe`) both inherit Invariable and carry `fundsSafu` (Depot additionally `noSupplyIncrease`). TractorFacet, which executes an arbitrary `AdvancedFarmCall[]` batch via `LibFarm._advancedFarm` (facet.delegatecall) AS THE PUBLISHER (LibTractor._user() returns blueprint.publisher inside the diamond), does NOT inherit Invariable (`contract TractorFacet` with no base) and its `tractor()` entrypoint carries only `verifyRequisition` + `runBlueprint`. It is the sole fund-executing batch entrypoint with no wrapper-level `fundsSafu`/flow guard. This is an asymmetric, incomplete guard relative to the otherwise-uniform Invariable architecture documented in Invariable.sol ('Every external writing function should use as many non-redundant invariant modifiers as possible. Excepting Diamond functions.').
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth solvency loss on the tractor path. Each inner delegatecall into a guarded facet (deposit/withdraw/convert/claim) re-checks `fundsSafu` at its own boundary, so a single inner call cannot leave the protocol insolvent. The residual exposure is that tractor executes a publisher-authorized batch with no batch-level net check: any unguarded inner sink reachable through a blueprint (a facet selector that moves funds but lacks `fundsSafu` itself), or an interleaving that is solvent at each inner checkpoint yet net-adverse across the batch, would execute with the publisher's delegated context and no final solvency assertion. FarmFacet closes exactly this gap with a wrapper `fundsSafu`; Tractor cannot because it does not inherit Invariable.
findings.proof_of_concept:
Guard-family comparison (batch / arbitrary-call execution entrypoints):
  FarmFacet.farm(bytes[])              -> [fundsSafu, withEth]            (Invariable)
  FarmFacet.advancedFarm(...)          -> [fundsSafu, withEth]            (Invariable)
  DepotFacet.pipe / multiPipe /
             advancedPipe / etherPipe  -> [fundsSafu, noSupplyIncrease]  (Invariable)
  TractorFacet.tractor(...)            -> [verifyRequisition, runBlueprint]   <- NO fundsSafu, NOT Invariable

Inheritance check:
  grep 'contract TractorFacet' -> 'contract TractorFacet {'   (no `is Invariable`)
  All other fund-executing facets: `... is Invariable`.

tractor() body (TractorFacet.sol L86-124): decodes blueprint into AdvancedFarmCall[] and runs each via LibFarm._advancedFarm -> _farm -> facet.delegatecall(data) under LibTractor._setPublisher(publisher). No fundsSafu/noOutFlow wraps the batch.

ite.intent: Preserve the uniform Invariable solvency net across every fund-executing entrypoint, including the publisher-delegated tractor batch
ite.technique: TractorFacet is declared without `is Invariable`, so tractor() cannot and does not apply fundsSafu; the only guards are signature/nonce/time. The wrapper-level solvency assertion that FarmFacet uses is absent on the equivalent Tractor batch path.
ite.evasion: Operator submits a publisher-signed blueprint whose AdvancedFarmCall[] either reaches a fund-moving facet selector that itself lacks fundsSafu, or composes guarded calls in an order solvent at each inner checkpoint but net-adverse across the batch; no batch-level fundsSafu fires.

ice_chain.corrupted_state: Beanstalk token solvency invariant (balances[i] >= entitlements[i]) is not asserted at the tractor batch boundary
ice_chain.impact: Potential protocol-level under-collateralization executed under a publisher's delegated context without a batch-level solvency revert; concrete fund loss depends on whether a reachable inner sink lacks its own fundsSafu
ice_chain.exploit_path: tractor(blueprint) -> _setPublisher(publisher) -> for each AdvancedFarmCall: facet.delegatecall -> [no wrapper fundsSafu] -> _resetPublisher. Confirming/denying impact requires enumerating every diamond selector reachable from a blueprint and proving each fund-moving one carries its own fundsSafu; that selector-completeness proof is not closeable from source alone, so this is routed for human verification rather than cleared.

findings.title: SiloFacet safeTransferFrom/safeBatchTransferFrom omit sibling's nonReentrant
findings.recommendation: For guard-architecture consistency, add nonReentrant to safeTransferFrom and safeBatchTransferFrom to match transferDeposit/transferDeposits. Functionally redundant (the callee transferDeposit is already nonReentrant on the shared diamond slot) but removes an audit ambiguity.
findings.description: Within SiloFacet the deposit-transfer group has asymmetric reentrancy guarding. `transferDeposit` (public, L140) and `transferDeposits` (external, L173) carry `fundsSafu noNetFlow noSupplyChange nonReentrant`. The ERC1155-standard siblings `safeTransferFrom` (L211) and `safeBatchTransferFrom` (L237) carry `fundsSafu noNetFlow noSupplyChange` but OMIT `nonReentrant`. They are in the same semantic group (move deposits/stalk between accounts).
findings.impact: None exploitable. Both functions immediately route to `transferDeposit(...)`, which is itself `nonReentrant` and backed by the SHARED diamond reentrancy slot (s.sys.reentrantStatus). Any reentry attempt during the transfer is caught by the inner guard. The functions perform no external token transfer or callback of their own (deposits are internal accounting; no ERC1155 acceptance-hook callback to the recipient is invoked). The omission is a guard-consistency blemish, not a reachable reentrancy.
findings.proof_of_concept:
Group: SiloFacet deposit-transfer functions
  transferDeposit(...)        -> [fundsSafu, noNetFlow, noSupplyChange, nonReentrant]   (L140)
  transferDeposits(...)       -> [fundsSafu, noNetFlow, noSupplyChange, nonReentrant]   (L173)
  safeTransferFrom(...)       -> [fundsSafu, noNetFlow, noSupplyChange]                 (L217)  <- no nonReentrant
  safeBatchTransferFrom(...)  -> [fundsSafu, noNetFlow, noSupplyChange]                 (L243)  <- no nonReentrant
Both safe* call transferDeposit which re-acquires nonReentrant on the shared diamond slot.

ite.intent: Apply the same nonReentrant guard to every external deposit-transfer entrypoint
ite.technique: safe* variants rely on the callee transferDeposit's guard rather than declaring their own; the asymmetry is cosmetic because the shared reentrant slot is set by the inner call
ite.evasion: No viable evasion: no external callback path exists in safe* before/after the guarded inner call

ice_chain.corrupted_state: none (reentry blocked by inner transferDeposit nonReentrant on the shared s.sys.reentrantStatus slot)

findings.disproof: safeTransferFrom/safeBatchTransferFrom contain no external call or recipient acceptance-hook before delegating to transferDeposit, which is `public ... nonReentrant`. The nonReentrant flag lives in shared diamond storage (s.sys.reentrantStatus), so a reentry into any nonReentrant silo/convert function during the transfer reverts. No state slot is mutated outside the inner guarded call. Therefore no reentrancy is reachable through these entrypoints; the missing modifier is redundant given the callee guard.

findings.title: ClaimFacet mow/mowMultiple and setApprovalForAll omit sibling's nonReentrant
findings.recommendation: Add nonReentrant to mow, mowMultiple and setApprovalForAll to match the rest of their facet groups. Functionally redundant (no external call inside these bodies and noNetFlow already constrains balances/stalk) but restores guard symmetry.
findings.description: Two intra-facet guard asymmetries in the same semantic group. ClaimFacet: `claimPlenty`/`claimAllPlenty`/`plant` carry `nonReentrant`, but `mow` (L116) and `mowMultiple` (L124) carry only `fundsSafu noNetFlow noSupplyChange` (no nonReentrant). ApprovalFacet: `approveDeposit`/`increaseDepositAllowance`/`decreaseDepositAllowance`/`permitDeposit(s)` all carry `nonReentrant`, but `setApprovalForAll` (L189) carries only `fundsSafu noNetFlow noSupplyChange` (no nonReentrant).
findings.impact: None exploitable. mow/mowMultiple perform only internal stalk/seed accounting (LibSilo._mow) with no external call where a reentry could observe inconsistent state and no token outflow (guarded by noNetFlow). setApprovalForAll writes a single approval mapping slot with no external interaction. The noNetFlow modifier already asserts token balances and stalk are unchanged across the call. Guard-consistency blemish, not a reachable issue.
findings.proof_of_concept:
ClaimFacet group:
  claimPlenty(...)     -> [..., nonReentrant]
  claimAllPlenty(...)  -> [..., nonReentrant]
  plant()              -> [..., nonReentrant]
  mow(...)             -> [fundsSafu, noNetFlow, noSupplyChange]   <- no nonReentrant
  mowMultiple(...)     -> [fundsSafu, noNetFlow, noSupplyChange]   <- no nonReentrant
ApprovalFacet group:
  approveDeposit / increase/decreaseDepositAllowance / permitDeposit(s) -> [..., nonReentrant]
  setApprovalForAll(...) -> [fundsSafu, noNetFlow, noSupplyChange]  <- no nonReentrant

ite.intent: Apply nonReentrant uniformly across each facet's state-mutating group
ite.technique: mow/setApprovalForAll rely on noNetFlow + absence of external calls instead of nonReentrant
ite.evasion: No external-call/callback exists in these functions to leverage for reentry

ice_chain.corrupted_state: none (no external call inside mow/mowMultiple/setApprovalForAll; noNetFlow enforces balance/stalk invariance)

findings.disproof: mow/mowMultiple call only LibSilo._mow which is pure internal stalk/seed accounting (no token transfer, no external call, no ERC777/1155 hook). setApprovalForAll writes one mapping entry. The noNetFlow modifier (present on all three) asserts watched token balances are unchanged and stalk does not decrease across the call, closing the only state a reentry could profit from. With no external interaction inside the function body, no reentry is reachable; the missing nonReentrant is redundant.

findings.title: Reseed L2 init functions are external with no access modifier
findings.recommendation: Verify via the diamondCut wiring / deployment script that no Reseed*.init selector is registered as a live facet and that diamondCut is owner-gated. As defense-in-depth, guard each init with onlyOwner / LibDiamond.enforceIsContractOwner or an initializer one-shot flag so the most state-powerful functions are not the least guarded even if accidentally registered.
findings.description: Every live Beanstalk facet is guarded (Invariable + nonReentrant + role/owner where applicable). By contrast all L2 reseed initializers — ReseedSilo.init, ReseedField.init, ReseedBarn.init, ReseedBean.init, ReseedInternalBalances.init, ReseedSun.init, ReseedWhitelist.init — are declared `external` with NO access modifier (no onlyOwner, no LibDiamond.enforceIsContractOwner, no initializer). They perform privileged bulk global-state writes (per-account stalk/roots/deposits, global silo balances, field pods, fertilizer linked list). This is the maximal guard asymmetry in the codebase: the most state-powerful functions are the least guarded. In the standard EIP-2535 pattern these run once via diamondCut's _init delegatecall and their selectors are not added as facets, so they are not attacker-callable post-upgrade. The risk is contingent: if any init selector is mistakenly registered on the diamond, or diamondCut is itself reachable, an attacker re-runs init to re-write global accounting.
findings.impact: If reachable as a live selector: permissionless re-execution of migration accounting (re-mint stalk/roots via the DT-001/DT-003 paths, re-zero global silo balances via DT-002), i.e. unbacked governance weight, stolen earned-Bean share, and accounting desync — Critical class. If correctly one-shot via diamondCut _init (expected), not externally reachable and the guard asymmetry is by-design for diamond initializers. Severity recorded as Medium pending the deployment/diamondCut wiring proof; cannot be cleared from source alone.
findings.proof_of_concept:
Guard comparison (state-write power vs guards):
  SiloFacet.deposit/withdraw      -> [fundsSafu, noSupplyChange, oneOutFlow, mowSender, nonReentrant]
  ConvertFacet.convert            -> [fundsSafu, noSupplyChange, nonReentrant]
  ReseedSilo.init(...)            -> []   (external, no modifier)  <- writes per-account stalk/roots + global silo balances
  ReseedField.init(...)          -> []   (external, no modifier)  <- writes field pods
  ReseedBarn.init()/mintFertilizers -> [] (external, no modifier)  <- writes fertilizer linked list
  ReseedBean / ReseedSun / ReseedWhitelist / ReseedInternalBalances .init -> [] (external, no modifier)
No onlyOwner / enforceIsContractOwner / initializer on any reseed init.

ite.intent: Restrict privileged one-shot migration accounting writes to the diamond owner / diamondCut init path
ite.technique: init functions ship with no access modifier, relying entirely on diamondCut wiring (one-shot delegatecall, selectors not registered) to be unreachable
ite.evasion: If an init selector is registered as a facet, or diamondCut is reachable by a non-owner, replay init to rewrite global stalk/roots/deposits

ice_chain.corrupted_state: s.accts[*].stalk/roots/deposits, s.sys.silo.balances[*], s.sys.fields[*].pods, s.sys.fert.* (all bulk-rewritable if init is callable)
ice_chain.impact: Unbacked stalk/roots + accounting desync if init is reachable post-deploy
ice_chain.exploit_path: ATTACKER -> reseedX.init(crafted args) [ONLY IF selector registered or diamondCut reachable] -> overwrites global accounting -> downstream silo/governance consumers read corrupted state. Reachability cannot be proven from source; routed for human verification of the diamondCut/deploy wiring (overlaps ACCESS-001).
